usage_note: Literally "be well": the everyday greeting when you meet someone (not for goodbye). It is said with the palms pressed together at the chest and a slight bow, the ນົບ (nop).
notes: A5 first note. ນົບ checked on English Wiktionary (verb: salute with palms pressed together); not in words.csv. | 2026-11-19 native (Na, Q0028): only when meeting

usage_note: Rice, and by extension a meal: ກິນເຂົ້າ ("eat rice") means "have a meal". The general word for food is ອາຫານ.
notes: A5 first note. ກິນ (W000018) and ອາຫານ (W000028) are in words.csv; ກິນເຂົ້າ is not a row of its own.

usage_note: Lao says what you are hungry for: ຫິວເຂົ້າ (literally "hungry for rice", that is, for a meal) is how you say "hungry", and ຫິວນ້ຳ means "thirsty". A native speaker tells us that "I'm hungry" with ຫິວ alone sounds unfinished: hungry for what?
notes: PLAN L1d (c). Native speaker 2026-11-13 (via owner): bare ຂ້ອຍຫິວ sounds incomplete; say ຫິວເຂົ້າ / ຫິວນ້ຳ. ຫິວນ້ຳ and ຢາກນ້ຳ both said (Na, Q0010). Wording by agent. No respellings in the text (LESSON_RULES 13, curriculum review).

usage_note: ໂຮງ is a building or hall used for one purpose, so ໂຮງໝໍ is the doctor's building. It is not ຫ້ອງ (a room). The same ໂຮງ starts ໂຮງຮຽນ (school).
notes: Owner 2026-11-19 asked for hospital; ໂຮງ is not taught as a word of its own (rare alone, and a homograph 'coffin' on Wiktionary). Meaning 'building, premises' from Wiktionary ໂຮງ; ໂຮງຮຽນ W000175. Wording by agent.

usage_note: Two parts you have seen: ເຂົ້າ, spelled and said like ເຂົ້າ 'rice' (here it is another word, 'enter'), and ໃຈ 'heart, mind', the ໃຈ of ຂອບໃຈ. So 'understand' is 'enter the mind'.
notes: CURRICULUM_PATH lesson 20 word note (ເຂົ້າ as in rice, ໃຈ as in ຂອບໃຈ). 'Enter the mind' from the words.csv pron_tip (Wiktionary ເຂົ້າໃຈ). ໃຈ W000007, ເຂົ້າ 'enter' W001425 (not taught). Wording by agent.

usage_note: ຢາກ ends in ກ, the same k you know from ກິນ, but at the end of a syllable it is cut off: the tongue closes for the k and the sound stops there, with no pop. Put ຢາກ before a verb: ຢາກກິນ 'want to eat'.
notes: CURRICULUM_PATH lesson 21 (owner: final ກ has no card of its own; this first word with it says so). Sound from letters.csv C01 pron_tip (verified: final k̚ unreleased). Wording by agent.

usage_note: ໄດ້ comes after the verb: ໄປໄດ້ 'can go'. For 'can't', ບໍ່ goes just before ໄດ້: ໄປບໍ່ໄດ້ 'can't go'. On its own, ໄດ້ answers 'OK' and ບໍ່ໄດ້ 'no, you can't'.
notes: CURRICULUM_PATH lesson 22 card (ໄດ້ after the verb, ບໍ່ before ໄດ້), as a word note. Pattern from S000000198 ຂ້ອຍໄປບໍ່ໄດ້ and S000002932; the bare-ໄດ້ answer is the agent's (D0004). Wording by agent.

usage_note: 'My mother' is mother + I: ແມ່ຂ້ອຍ. The person it belongs to comes after: ແມ່ເຈົ້າ 'your mother'. Watch the look-alike: ແມ່ນ 'is' has a ນ at the end; ແມ່ 'mother' has none.
notes: CURRICULUM_PATH lesson 23 card ('my mother' = mother + I) and the planned look-alike contrast ແມ່ / ແມ່ນ (W000004), as a word note. Possessor-after-noun from S000000063, S000000062. Wording by agent.

usage_note: Watch the look-alike: ນ້ອງ 'younger sibling' ends in ງ (ng), ນ້ອຍ 'small' ends in ຍ (y). Lao also calls anyone younger than you ນ້ອງ, a friendly way to address them.
notes: CURRICULUM_PATH planned contrast ນ້ອງ / ນ້ອຍ (W000090). Address use (calling a younger person, e.g. a waiter, ນ້ອງ) is the agent's knowledge: unverified. Wording by agent.

usage_note: ໂຮງ 'building', as in ໂຮງໝໍ 'hospital', + ຮຽນ 'study': the building for studying.
notes: CURRICULUM_PATH lesson 24 word note (ໂຮງ as in ໂຮງໝໍ). ໂຮງ meaning as in the W000172 note. Wording by agent.
